headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading error: Copilot can modify repo state while gpt-researcher can write broad documents and use external APIs, creating unsafe handoff paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while gpt-researcher can produce Markdown, Word, and other documents plus use MCP. If B’s outputs are pasted or stored in shared files, A may treat attacker-controlled text as trusted instructions. This is not provably blocked by either profile, but it is not a default direct channel.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher outputs are copied into files that Copilot reads as repo context
IF either agent ingests the other’s generated text without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep B outputs in a separate workspace folder
Require manual review before Copilot consumes any B-generated text
Add a provenance header to B outputs
Disable automatic file watching for shared drafts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization/provenance filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open buffers and sends context to api.githubcopilot.com, while gpt-researcher reads local documents and can call broad external APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or documents can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or third-party services. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace by default, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or document set
IF sensitive source code or local documents are present in that shared workspace
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for code and research
Exclude secrets and private docs from B’s input set
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive repos
Review outbound API destinations for B
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write filesystem and modify git state, and gpt-researcher can read/write files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. If both operate on the same repo or directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The overlap is explicit in both profiles and dangerous in default collaborative use.
conditions: IF both agents are allowed to write to the same repository or working directory
IF git operations are not serialized by an external lock
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Serialize git writes with a lock file
Disable package installation in B for shared repos
Require human approval before commits
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot’s Workspace plans and applies edits, and gpt-researcher’s planner/execution/publisher pipeline can turn generated research into reports. If B’s output is fed into A or vice versa without verification, one agent can amplify the other’s mistakes into edits or published artifacts. The profiles show a direct handoff risk, and the blast radius includes incorrect code or reports.
conditions: IF one agent’s generated text is used as authoritative input to the other
IF no verification step checks claims before edits or publication
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require citations for any factual claims before reuse
Limit Copilot to proposing edits only
Limit gpt-researcher to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add automated claim verification

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is tied to GitHub repo context and vendor APIs, while gpt-researcher handles local documents and multiple third-party APIs plus secrets. If regulated data such as EU PII, confidential code, or internal documents enters both systems, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not specify a documented compliance alignment, so the safer reading is a medium mismatch risk.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or confidential documents are processed by both agents
IF retention or residency requirements differ between GitHub Copilot and gpt-researcher’s configured APIs
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to either agent
Check vendor DPAs and retention settings
Use redacted inputs for research tasks
Separate EU and non-EU datasets
requires-engineering: formalize a data-processing policy for the pair
